content.thinking: I'm weighing the timing here—the flag was toggled before the onset, which points toward feature-flag-toggle, but the fact that totals are already written wrong in the store of record pushes me to reconsider silent-data-corruption as the real root cause, since a flag move alone doesn't always explain corrupted data already persisted.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: Shopper spend totals written since 2026-10-18T18:54:00Z disagree with the purchases behind them (240 of 240 are wrong, the widest by 1,297.31). This began two minutes after the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on at 2026-10-18T18:52:00Z. The service itself serves normally and every metric is flat, so the stored totals are what is wrong.

supporting_evidence.claim: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on (actor: admin)
240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them; oldest affected purchase recorded at 2026-10-18T18:54:00Z
error_rate, latency, memory and cpu are flat across the whole metrics window, with cpu_limit_cores at 3.0 throughout
The rollout has converged with no deployment in the history, so the flag is the only change near the onset.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: Switching monthly-spend-feature on at 2026-10-18T18:52:00Z changed how spend totals are computed, and the totals have been wrong since then. This is the same flag change as the first explanation, read as a pure behaviour change.

supporting_evidence.claim: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
The oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-10-18T18:54:00Z, two minutes after the flag moved.
